ig_caption:
Kubernetes Service not working? Check the endpoints 🔌

Both pods Running. The Service exists. Every request fails (connection refused).

kubectl get endpoints → <none>. The Service has no pods behind it.
⚠️ pods are labelled app: checkout
⚠️ the Service selector says app: check-out
One dash. It matches nothing, and Kubernetes never warns you.

The fix:
✅ make the selector match the pod labels exactly
✅ when traffic fails, check endpoints first

→ 2 endpoints, the request goes through.

In Kubernetes, labels are the wiring.

Share this with your K8s team 🔁 Follow for more Kubernetes breaks.

#kubernetes #k8s #devops #networking #sre
yt_title: Kubernetes Service has no endpoints: the one-dash bug #kubernetes
yt_description:
Real run on a local kind cluster: pods Running, Service created, requests get "connection refused".
kubectl get endpoints checkout → <none>, because the Service selector (app: check-out) doesn't match the pod label (app: checkout).
Fix: selector must match pod labels exactly → 2 endpoints, requests succeed.

Debug order for "Service not working": endpoints → selector vs labels → targetPort.

Series: Kubernetes in production, what breaks (live). Follow for more.
